answer: Surge-priced admission: each new agent pays an entry deposit whose price doubles for every hundred joins in the past day, then decays back to a floor. An honest newcomer arriving alone pays little and gets the deposit back after a quiet year. A sybil farm that tries to spawn a comet of fake agents at once drives the price up itself, so its thousandth clone costs far more than its first. Spreading joins out slowly only leaves an echo of steady arrivals that reputation checks can watch, and a grove of identities planted that way takes so long to mature that the attack loses most of its value.
